To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a payload based intrusion detector, we call it PAYL, for network traffic.

(a) a simple, fully automatic and unsupervised payload based anomaly detector can be very effecient, accurate, and effective; and (b) the method is very effecient in that it can handle a high rate of traffic, and is very accurate in that it has very few false positives and very few false negatives.

(i) the application payload is an excellent source of information for anomaly detection; (ii) the byte frequency distribution of the payload is a very effective and efficient model; and (iii) the Mahalanobis Distance is a simple and effective way to detect deviations from the model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues.
the following questions: 1. Can we detect network attacks without the help of signatures?
the development of anomaly detectors that can be used for network intrusion detection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PAYL method is an extremely effective anomaly based network intrusion detection system for application layer traffic, such as web, ftp and telnet.
PAYL has a high detection rate and very few false positives, which is a good combination for any IDS.
PAYL is a simple, fast and effective payload based anomaly detection system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PAYL is the first payload based network anomaly detector that can detect a wide range of attacks with a very low false positive rate.
we present the first fully unsupervised, automatic and very efficient payload based anomaly detector.
PAYL is a simple and effective payload based anomaly detector that can be used in a wide range of applications, such as IDS, malware detection, spam detection, and so on.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the payload can be modeled very accurately using a simple byte frequency distribution.
a fully unsupervised, automatic method can perform well on real world data.
the payload of network traffic can be used to detect anomalies in an unsupervised fashion with very low false positive rates.
